hooks.name: mob_spawn_placement_check
hooks.doc: NeoForge's `MobSpawnEvent.SpawnPlacementCheck`: may the entity type `kind` spawn at `pos` for `reason`? It is asked after vanilla's own spawn predicate (`SpawnPlacements.checkSpawnRules`: light, the ground it needs, the biome, slime chunks, the peaceful rule) has run: `default_result` is what it answered, and `result` starts as `Default`, which keeps that answer. Set `Succeed` or `Fail` to force the check. It runs wherever the game calls `checkSpawnRules` with the game's level: natural spawning, a village siege's zombies, a patrol, a zombie's reinforcements, a spawner and a trial spawner. A spawner whose spawn data carries custom spawn rules never reaches it, as in NeoForge. The predicate always runs first, as `default_result` is its answer, so its random draws are vanilla's whatever a mod answers; a listener should be a pure function of its inputs, because the checks run again when a tick is replayed. The host is the read-only one: a listener reads the world and writes nothing. Not told of `/summon` or a spawn egg, which do not check placements. Server-side. Beyond NeoForge: one `NativeSpawnCheck` answers this event and `mob_spawn_position_check`, which NeoForge gives two nested enums with the same three constants.

hooks.name: mob_spawn_position_check
hooks.doc: NeoForge's `MobSpawnEvent.PositionCheck`: may the freshly created mob of type `kind` stand at `pos` (its position, a mob's centre) for `reason`? Vanilla's two checks are `Mob.checkSpawnRules` (the type's own rules) and `Mob.checkSpawnObstruction` (inside blocks or fluids, an ocelot's grass and sea level). `result` starts as `Default`, which runs them; `Succeed` or `Fail` answers instead and they are skipped. It runs on natural spawning, chunk generation's creature packs and spawner blocks (where a spawner with custom spawn rules skips `Mob.checkSpawnRules` on `Default`, as vanilla and NeoForge do).  A trial spawner runs only `checkSpawnObstruction`, so only that is skipped. Server-side. With no listener or `Default` the checks and their random draws are vanilla's; `Succeed` and `Fail` skip the checks and so their draws (NeoForge's contract), and the level random's order changes only then; a listener should be a pure function of its inputs, because ticks are replayed.
